specification.problem: Simon's problem for n=2: given black-box access to f:\{0,1\}^2\to\{0,1\}^2 with the promise that f(x)=f(y) iff y\in\{x, x\oplus s\} for a hidden string s, determine s using O(n) quantum queries. The abstract reports a one-way (measurement-based) optical implementation on a five-qubit cluster state; this specification reconstructs the logical two-qubit algorithm in the circuit model with one explicit oracle instance.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scope (chosen by the agent, no experiment_scope supplied): the gate-model logical two-qubit Simon algorithm (2 input qubits + 2 output qubits), a single explicit oracle instance with s=11, f(x1,x2)=(0, x1\oplus x2), the resulting measurement distribution, and the classical linear-algebra postprocessing. Outside scope: the specific five-qubit cluster-state graph, the single-qubit measurement-basis choices that encode each black box, the set of 'key representative functions' queried in the experiment, the optical setup, the experimental data, and the n-qubit resource analysis.

symbols.meaning: number of input bits of the black-box function (n=2 in scope)
n-bit strings; x is the oracle input, y the output register content, z the measured input-register outcome
hidden period (XOR mask) of Simon's problem

equations.label: Simon's promise
equations.description: Defines the black-box period-finding problem: f is 2-to-1 with XOR period s (or 1-to-1 if s=0^n); the task is to find s.
equations.abstract_quote: Simon’s Problem - a black box period-finding problem
equations.justification: The abstract names Simon's problem as a black-box period-finding problem; this is the standard statement of its promise, recalled from background knowledge.
assumptions: The experiment uses the standard formulation of Simon's problem.

equations.label: Oracle unitary
equations.description: Standard reversible black box acting on an n-qubit input register and an n-qubit output register.
equations.justification: Textbook oracle model for Simon's algorithm; the abstract does not specify how the black box is realized beyond 'modifying the bases of single-qubit measurements'.
assumptions: Register ordering |x\rangle|y\rangle with x_1 (leftmost) the most significant bit.

equations.label: State after H, U_f, H
equations.description: Exact state of the 2n-qubit system before measurement in the circuit-model Simon algorithm.
equations.justification: Direct algebraic consequence of eq_2 and H|x_i\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt2}\sum_{z_i}(-1)^{x_i z_i}|z_i\rangle.

equations.label: Output distribution on the input register
equations.description: Measuring the input register in the computational basis yields a uniformly random z orthogonal (mod 2) to s; the output register need not be measured.
equations.justification: Follows from eq_3 and eq_1: terms x and x\oplus s share |f(x)\rangle and their amplitudes (-1)^{x\cdot z}(1+(-1)^{s\cdot z}) cancel unless s\cdot z=0. For s=0^n the distribution is uniform over all z.

equations.label: Explicit n=2 oracle instance
equations.description: One tiny concrete black box satisfying eq_1 with s=11, realized by two CNOTs onto output qubit y_2; the resulting outcome distribution is on z\in\{00,11\}.
equations.justification: Chosen as the smallest explicit instance; the abstract mentions 'key representative functions' but does not list them, so this instance is not claimed to be one actually used in the experiment.
assumptions: This instance is the agent's choice, not taken from the abstract.
Output qubit y_1 is left in |0\rangle and could be omitted for this instance.

equations.label: Classical postprocessing for n=2
equations.latex: \text{given measured } z\neq 00:\quad s = \text{the unique } s'\in\{01,10,11\}\text{ with } z\cdot s'\equiv 0 \pmod 2;\qquad \text{for } n=2:\; z=11\Rightarrow s=11,\; z=01\Rightarrow s=10,\; z=10\Rightarrow s=01
equations.description: For n=2 a single nonzero outcome determines s (under the promise s\neq 0); in general one collects n-1 linearly independent z and solves the homogeneous system over GF(2). The outcome z=00 is uninformative and the run is repeated.
equations.justification: Standard Gaussian elimination over GF(2) on the constraints z^{(k)}\cdot s = 0; for n=2 the nullspace of a single nonzero z has exactly one nonzero element.
assumptions: Promise s\neq 00 (2-to-1 case); otherwise s=00 is concluded only statistically after observing outcomes spanning all of \{0,1\}^2.

registers.name: input (query) register
registers.role: holds x; Hadamard-transformed before and after the oracle; measured in computational basis to obtain z

registers.name: output (function) register
registers.role: holds y\oplus f(x); entangled with the input register by U_f; not measured (or its result discarded)

specification.initial_state: |0\rangle_{x_1}|0\rangle_{x_2}|0\rangle_{y_1}|0\rangle_{y_2} = |00\rangle_{\mathrm{in}}|00\rangle_{\mathrm{out}}, ordering |x_1 x_2\rangle|y_1 y_2\rangle with x_1 the most significant input bit

steps.description: Apply H to each input qubit to create the uniform superposition \frac12\sum_x |x\rangle|00\rangle.
Apply the oracle U_f (for the explicit instance: CNOT from x_1 to y_2 then CNOT from x_2 to y_2).
Apply H to each input qubit again, yielding the state of eq_3.
Measure the input register in the computational basis; outcome z satisfies z\cdot s = 0 mod 2 with the distribution of eq_4 (eq_5 for the instance). Repeat until a nonzero z is obtained.
Classically infer s from the nonzero outcome(s) by solving the GF(2) linear system.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis (Z) measurement of the two input-register qubits after the final Hadamards; outcome z\in\{0,1\}^2 distributed per eq_4. The output register is not measured. Runs are repeated to obtain a nonzero z and to estimate the outcome histogram for comparison with the ideal distribution.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Solve z\cdot s \equiv 0 (mod 2) over GF(2) for the nonzero s (eq_6); for n=2 one nonzero outcome suffices. Experimentally, compare the measured outcome frequencies with the ideal probabilities 1/2 on the two allowed outcomes and 0 on the forbidden ones (eq_4, eq_5).
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the agent chose the gate-model logical two-qubit Simon algorithm with the single oracle instance s=11, f(x)=(0,x_1\oplus x_2) as the smallest useful construction.

The paper's one-way implementation is assumed to be logically equivalent to the circuit of eq_3 (the abstract says the black box is selected by 'modifying the bases of single-qubit measurements on a five-qubit cluster state'), but the actual cluster graph and measurement pattern are not reconstructed.
Standard oracle model U_f|x\rangle|y\rangle=|x\rangle|y\oplus f(x)\rangle and standard Simon promise are assumed.
